thread:
alice_sre: quick addendum to the RCA we sent earlier — customer asked for a concise timeline + confirmation of mitigations. copying the thread here so we can draft a single customer-friendly note.
ben_cs: thanks. i can draft a short customer-facing summary. do we want to offer a proactive SLA credit or just apologies + remediation steps first?
carlos_eng: from eng side — root cause was an autoscaler edge-case where pending cold-start requests briefly routed to a stale scheduling bucket. fixed in canary at 09:12 UTC and rolled to prod at 09:28 UTC. impact window ~09:03–09:27 UTC. no data loss, only increased error/latency for generation endpoints.
dana_pm: timeline sounds right but we should be careful with exact seconds. customer asked for request-level examples; we should avoid revealing internal IPs. a high-level timeline and what we changed is fine.
emma_support: customer reported first at 09:10 UTC via support ticket. they escalated to account team at 09:18. they were impacted by 5-minute spikes and some 500s. linking ticket #5432.
incident-bot: INCIDENT 2021-09-03-01 acknowledged by @alice_sre at 09:05 UTC. Pager routed to SRE on-call. Status page updated to "Degraded performance" at 09:07 UTC.
alice_sre: ok i'm going to propose two artifacts: 1) short customer summary (one paragraph + TL;DR bullet), 2) appendix timeline for technical teams. ben — can you draft the paragraph? i'll add timeline and mitigations.
ben_cs: draft customer note below — feedback welcome:

"TL;DR: On 2021-09-03 between ~09:03–09:27 UTC some requests to Redwood hosted inference experienced elevated latency and intermittent errors. We identified an autoscaling scheduler issue causing some requests to be routed to a stale execution bucket. Our engineers deployed a fix at 09:28 UTC; normal service resumed and we've implemented additional guards to prevent recurrence. We apologize for the impact and are offering to review any affected usage and discuss an SLA credit if this incident caused measurable customer impact."

thoughts?
carlos_eng: good start. suggest adding a line: "No customer data was exposed or lost." also add that dedicated/private customers were unaffected by the scheduler path.
dana_pm: yes add that. also add next steps: "we're adding a canary assertion in the autoscaler and increasing observability on routing buckets." keep the offer for SLA credit conditional on measurable impact.
emma_support: polished draft for customer-facing email (short):

"Hi <Customer Name>,\n\nWe wanted to follow up about the disruption you experienced today between 09:03–09:27 UTC. During that window, a scheduling bug in our autoscaler caused a subset of requests to see higher latency and occasional errors. Our engineers deployed a resolution at 09:28 UTC and we verified service returned to normal.\n\nWhat we did: deployed a fix to the scheduler, added additional health checks and routing guards, and rolled monitoring alerts to detect similar anomalies faster.\n\nImpact: Some API requests to the hosted inference endpoints returned errors or timed out during the window. No customer data was exposed or lost. Dedicated and private deployments were not affected.\n\nNext steps: We’re conducting a post-incident review to harden the autoscaler and will share a short RCA. If you’d like, we can review your logs for affected requests and discuss SLA remediation.\n\nWe’re sorry for the disruption and are available to answer questions.\n\nBest,\nThe Redwood Support Team"

ben_cs: that reads well. emma — can you send to the customer once we lock timeline wording? also need a short status-page update copy.
emma_support: status page blurb suggestion: "Degraded performance observed between 09:03–09:27 UTC for some hosted inference requests due to an autoscaling scheduler issue. A fix was deployed at 09:28 UTC; services restored. Investigating root cause and next steps." short and matches email.
alice_sre: timeline appendix (technical):

"09:03 UTC — initial anomalous error spike begins on metric: generation_p50/latency and 5xx-rate for hosted-api-prod.
09:05 UTC — pager fired to on-call (alice_sre). initial triage pointed at routing timeouts.
09:10 UTC — customer support ticket #5432 received reporting failures.
09:12 UTC — engineering canary deploy with scheduler guard applied; error rate decreased in canary.
09:18 UTC — customer escalated via account team.
09:24 UTC — canary health dips due to backlog; further adjustments applied.
09:28 UTC — full prod rollout of scheduler fix and routing guard. metrics normalized by 09:35 UTC.
Post-incident — added assertion tests in autoscaler, increased metrics granularity for routing buckets, and created a runbook for similar symptoms."

carlos_eng: also logging change: capture scheduling-bucket-id in traces for 48h to correlate customer reports.
dana_pm: ok this is great. last bit — SLA credit language. proposed: "We’re prepared to provide a pro-rated SLA credit for impacted usage upon request; please reply if you’d like us to evaluate your usage during the incident window." keeps it optional.
emma_support: i'll include that line and send now. sending to <customer> in 5.
ben_cs: before send — minor edit to avoid technical jargon: replace "scheduling bucket" with "internal routing bucket" in customer note.
alice_sre: agreed. final QA check: does anyone object to sending now?
ben_cs: no objections.
car los_eng: typo — no objections either.

emma_support: sent to customer at 09:52 UTC. ticket updated with email copy. closing loop here — will post a follow-up when customer responds.

alice_sre: follow-up: we'll open a small postmortem doc and link it in the support ticket. expected preliminary RCA in 48 hours, full doc in 5 business days.

ben_cs: thanks everyone. i'll prepare a short internal comms blurb for CS leadership summarizing the offer and next steps.

incident-bot: REMINDER: Please ensure the incident postmortem checklist is completed and linked: https://redwood/doc/incident-checklist (owner: alice_sre).
